func testChangesAreListedAheadOfAWholeRootRescan() throws {
        for i in 0..<20 {
            try FileManager.default.createDirectory(atPath: dir + "/deep/d\(i)", withIntermediateDirectories: true)
        }
        let service = IndexService(roots: [dir], indexURL: URL(fileURLWithPath: dir + "-walk.bin"))
        service.sliceSeconds = 0 // one folder per slice
        service.stepsByHand = true // only the events below, listed slice by slice
        service.start()
        defer { service.stop() }
        let before = service.appliedEventId(for: dir) ?? 0
        func event(_ path: String, dropped: Bool = false, id: UInt64) -> Watcher.Event {
            Watcher.Event(path: path, mustScanSubDirs: dropped, rootChanged: false, historyDone: false,
                          dropped: dropped, id: id)
        }
        func count(_ q: String) -> Int { service.index.read { $0.search(Query.parse(q)).total } }

        service.receive([event("/", dropped: true, id: before + 10)], root: dir)
        service.flushSliceNow() // lists the root only; a, deep and empty are next
        XCTAssertEqual(service.foldersLeftToList, 3)

        // a/b/c is three folders below the top of the walk, so only its own event can list it now.
        FileManager.default.createFile(atPath: dir + "/a/b/c/fresh.txt", contents: nil)
        XCTAssertEqual(count("fresh.txt"), 0)
        service.receive([event(dir + "/a/b/c/", id: before + 20)], root: dir)
        service.flushSliceNow()
        XCTAssertEqual(count("fresh.txt"), 1, "a new change must not wait for the rescan")
        XCTAssertEqual(service.foldersLeftToList, 3, "the rescan is still under way")
        XCTAssertLessThan(service.appliedEventId(for: dir) ?? 0, before + 10,
                          "the cursor must not pass the dropped events before the rescan is done")

        // FSEvents asks for a subtree scan of a/b: listed now, not after the whole walk.
        FileManager.default.createFile(atPath: dir + "/a/b/c/subtree.txt", contents: nil)
        service.receive([Watcher.Event(path: dir + "/a/b/", mustScanSubDirs: true, rootChanged: false,
                                       historyDone: false, id: before + 25)], root: dir)
        service.flushSliceNow() // lists a/b
        service.flushSliceNow() // lists a/b/c
        XCTAssertEqual(count("subtree.txt"), 1)
        XCTAssertEqual(service.passesWaiting, 0)
        XCTAssertEqual(service.foldersLeftToList, 3, "the root walk is still under way")

        // Dropped again: queued as a second pass, not a restart that could never finish.
        service.receive([event("/", dropped: true, id: before + 30)], root: dir)
        service.flushSliceNow()
        XCTAssertEqual(service.passesWaiting, 1, "a restart would have dropped the first pass instead")
        XCTAssertGreaterThan(service.foldersLeftToList, 0)

        service.sync()
        XCTAssertEqual(service.foldersLeftToList, 0)
        XCTAssertEqual(service.passesWaiting, 0)
        XCTAssertGreaterThanOrEqual(service.appliedEventId(for: dir) ?? 0, before + 30)
        XCTAssertEqual(count("two.pdf"), 1)
        XCTAssertEqual(count("\"path:/deep/d\""), 20)
    }

# Round 2 dispositions (fixes in commit ce331f3)

- R6 (descendant MustScanSubDirs deferred behind a root walk): ACCEPTED. `enqueue` now defers only when the same target is already a walk target (`walkTargets.contains(target)`). A descendant request is pushed on top now (dedupes queued items inside it, joins walkTargets). Test added to testChangesAreListedAheadOfAWholeRootRescan (subtree scan of a/b during the root walk: listed in two slices, passesWaiting stays 0).
- R7 (a failure followed by a success still counts): ACCEPTED. `Scanner.refreshFailures(..., handled:)` reports each folder that did not fail (and drops an earlier failure of it from its own list). The service clears `walkFailures[path]` and `retries[path]` there. This replaces the old walkPaths-based reset, so "giving up" needs consecutive failed walks.
- R8 (tests race the real watcher and delayed flushes): ACCEPTED. `stepsByHand`, set before `start()`: no watchers (startWatcher returns), receive schedules no flush, no continuation, no retry timer. Both slice tests use it.
- R9 (a single 6 s folder listing or a >50K sort inside a slice): REJECTED for this PR. The slice bound is per folder by design; a slow folder (TCC-checked sandbox containers, ~6 s) or a sort bounds latency at a few seconds occasionally, a pre-existing cost that is not the measured bug (118 s walks). Moving listing or sorting off `work` changes the write-on-one-queue design; noted as a known limit for a follow-up. Measured on the Mac with the fix: every parity_check live step 0.1 to 0.8 s.

# Round 4 dispositions (fixes in the latest commit)

- R11 (in one slice, a recursive failure then a shallow success clears the retry count): ACCEPTED. Scanner calls `handled` only when it holds no remaining local failure for the folder. The test `testShallowListingDoesNotClearAFailedWalk` now also asserts `handled` is not called for it. The service rule for failures from earlier slices is unchanged (a deep success clears; a shallow one only clears a shallow failure).
- R12 (sustained drops keep nextPass non-empty, so the cursor never settles): ACCEPTED. Per-pass boundaries: when the walk empties and a next pass is promoted, `passStartIds` holds `walkEventIds` at that moment. When that promoted pass finishes, `settle(passStartIds)` accounts for the failures so far and applies those ids. Roots with failures move all their held ids (snapshot and later) to `pendingEventIds` and out of `walkEventIds`/`passStartIds`, and wait for the retry. `finishWalk` uses the same `settle(walkEventIds)`. Test `testCursorAdvancesPassByPassWhileDropsKeepComing`: drops during pass 1 and pass 2; after pass 2 the cursor equals the drop pass 2 covered; after sync, the last one.
- Note on settle at a pass boundary: re-queued retries are taken by the next continuation flush right away, not after 5 s, and handled within the same round. That keeps the cursor from passing them before they are retried.

input.content:
## Problem

Live updates sometimes took 40 to 120 s to show (parity_check on 2026-11-02: a new file after 43.8 s, a rename not seen after 60 s).

## Cause (measured on the Mac, 2.58M entries)

After a bulk operation (1000 to 5000 files created or removed at once), FSEvents sends `UserDropped | MustScanSubDirs` on `/`. The daemon then re-lists the whole root, and it did that in one go on the serial `work` queue. Every change made in the meantime waited for it to finish.

- Daemon log (diagnostic build): `re-listing all of /: events were dropped (event 681900361 on /)` at 23:41:40, then `refreshed / and below in 118.5 s` at 23:43:38.
- A separate FSEvents watcher saw `flags=0x3` on `/` at the same moments. `sample` showed `work` inside `flush -> refreshFailures` for the whole stall, and `lsof` showed the daemon listing all of `~`.
- The "new top-level folder" pattern was only ordering: in the test, that step always came right after the previous 2000-file removal.

## Fix

- `Scanner.refreshFailures(_:queue:cancelled:yield:handled:discovered:)` can stop part-way and continue later.
- `IndexService.flush` keeps the unfinished walk and works through it in 0.25 s slices on `work`. Changes that arrive between slices go on top, so they are listed first.
- After dropped events, the folders changed in the last minute are listed first: at most 64, newest first, including folders just created. A big delete overflows the queue with its own events, so the walk alone would find it minutes later.
- A repeat of the same whole-root walk (events dropped again) runs as a next pass instead of restarting. A subtree scan requested during a walk is listed right away.
- Cursor safety: the saved event id never passes an unapplied change.
  - Ids are held until the walk is done. Each finished pass applies what was taken in before it started.
  - Folders that failed keep their root's ids pending until they are retried.
  - A drive that comes back keeps its old volume id and cursor until its re-list is done.
  - Compaction waits for the walk, because the walk holds record ids. A full scan resets the walk.
- Retry accounting is unchanged in meaning. A folder's failure is cleared only by a later listing that covers it, and the 5 s retry timer no longer delays fresh changes.
- New log lines: why a whole root is re-listed, how long queued changes took (when over 2 s), and how long a save took.

## Tests (all run on CI)

- `testChangesAreListedAheadOfAWholeRootRescan`: a fresh change and a subtree scan are listed during a whole-root rescan, and the cursor stays behind the drop until the rescan is done. A repeated drop queues a next pass.
- `testRecentlyChangedFoldersAreListedFirstAfterDroppedEvents`: covers recently changed folders and just-created folders.
- `testCursorAdvancesPassByPassWhileDropsKeepComing`
- `testShallowListingDoesNotClearAFailedWalk`

The slice tests use `stepsByHand`, which turns off watchers and automatic flushes. On `main` these tests do not compile, because there is no resumable walk. Under the old flush, which ran everything in one go, their assertions would fail.

## Verified on the Mac

See the comment below for parity_check results with the fixed daemon installed.

## Known limits

- One slow folder listing still bounds a slice. Sandbox containers under `~/Library/Containers` take about 6 s each to list.
- The whole-volume walk (90 to 120 s of disk and CPU) still runs after every drop. A possible follow-up: on `UserDropped`, restart the stream from the last delivered id, so fseventsd might replay the dropped folder events from its on-disk log. Not verified.

input.message:
Stopping here because Eric is leaving. Everything is committed and pushed, CI is green, and the fixed daemon is installed and running. The `/mattpocock-skills:handoff` skill can only be started by the user, so Eric has to run it himself; I did not copy its workflow.

**Root cause.** After a bulk change (1000 to 5000 files created or deleted at once), FSEvents reports that it dropped events on `/`. The daemon then re-lists the whole volume (2.58M entries) on its single update queue, and every other change waits until that finishes.
- Daemon log (diagnostic build): `re-listing all of /: events were dropped (event 681900361 on /)` at 23:41:40, then `refreshed / and below in 118.5 s`.
- A separate FSEvents watcher saw the same dropped-events flag at the stall times. `sample` showed the update queue busy in that refresh for the whole stall, and `lsof` showed the daemon walking all of `~`.
- The "new top-level folder" pattern was only test ordering: that step always followed a 2000-file removal.
- None of your four leads was the cause. Saves were not involved, and `ev` was not reading a stale snapshot.

**The fix** (`Sources/EverythingCore/Scanner.swift`, `Sources/EverythingCore/Service.swift`):
- The whole-volume re-list now runs in 0.25 s slices. Changes that arrive in between are listed first.
- After dropped events, up to 64 folders changed in the last minute (including just-created ones) are listed before the long walk. Big deletes overflow FSEvents with their own events, so the walk alone would find them minutes later.
- If events are dropped again during a walk, another pass is queued instead of restarting the walk.
- The saved cursor never passes a change that has not been applied. Each finished pass advances it.
- New log lines say why the whole volume is being re-listed, how long queued changes took, and how long a save took.
- I added a Gotchas entry to `docs/STATUS.md`.

**Tests** (in `Tests/EverythingCoreTests/MacTests.swift`, all pass on CI, 55 tests total):
- `testChangesAreListedAheadOfAWholeRootRescan`
- `testRecentlyChangedFoldersAreListedFirstAfterDroppedEvents`
- `testCursorAdvancesPassByPassWhileDropsKeepComing`
- `testShallowListingDoesNotClearAFailedWalk`

On `main` they do not compile (the resumable walk they need does not exist there). They do not fail as such.

**parity_check results with the fix installed:**
- Before: 43.8 s, more than 60 s, 15.8 s and 20.8 s on the first steps.
- Build 2c8f86e, the last set with a quiet machine: 3 runs, all `0 failed`. One earlier timestamped run on the build before it was also clean: all 5000-file creates and deletes at 0.1 to 0.3 s, with 11 dropped-event notices during the run.
- Final build 51bf3fe, now installed: the machine was heavily loaded by other work (load average 12.5, `trustd` at 85% CPU). Out of 5 complete runs, 1 had no failures.
  - Run 3 of the first set: `delete 1000 files at once` took 7.0 s and 5.8 s.
  - Run 1 of the second set: deletes of 50 and 1000 files and a 2500-file create took 5.1 to 6.3 s.
  - The search-speed checks also failed in most runs, at 100 to 730 ms against a 100 ms limit. The search code did not change, so I read that as load.

Before the fix the same cases took 60 s or more. Under load, a bulk delete whose own events were dropped still takes about 5 to 7 s. The 0.25 s slicing itself is in every tested build; the final build adds only cursor bookkeeping and the 64-folder cap.

**Daemon state.**
- Fixed daemon (51bf3fe; the later commit f425c7f changes only tests) is installed at `~/.local/bin/everythingd` and running: ready, 2.59M entries.
- Signed with "MacEverything Local Signing", identifier `com.erash11.maceverything.daemon`. The requirement matched the original, so Full Disk Access holds.
- The original binary is kept at `~/.local/bin/everythingd.pre-livefix-2026-11-02`.
- `ev` was not reinstalled; it did not change.
- Test folders are cleaned up.

**PR.** https://github.com/erash11/MacEverything/pull/12, head f425c7f, CI green. Not merged. I did not touch `ci.yml`. I did not post the parity-results comment the PR description promises; the numbers above can go there.

**Codex review.** 5 rounds, the cap, plus one extra round that failed because I edited a file mid-run; it did not count. Findings R1 to R8 and R10 to R12 were accepted and fixed. R9 was rejected: a single slow folder (about 6 s for sandbox containers) still bounds one slice, which is recorded as a known limit. Round 5 still said REVISE: the R13 (cursor for a re-plugged drive) and R14 (cap on recent folders) fixes were made after it and are **unreviewed**. Run log: `~/.claude/jobs/a21541bc/tmp/codex-review/`.

**Not verified.**
- The external-drive paths: CRASHBOX was unplugged, so the returning-drive change is checked by reasoning only.
- A clean 3-of-3 parity set on the final build.
- The whole-volume walk (90 to 120 s of disk and CPU) still runs after every drop. A possible follow-up: restart the stream from the last delivered event id on a drop, which might replay the lost events instead.

**Next step.** On a quiet machine, run `python3 -I /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Personal/MacEverything/scripts/parity_check.py` 3 times, then merge #12. To roll back: `mv /Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/everythingd.pre-livefix-2026-11-02 /Users/kristinarash/.local/bin/everythingd`, then `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.erash11.maceverything.daemon`.
